data.name: MOD0001_Title
data.value: A module must not expose public types

data.name: MOD0001_Message
data.value: Type '{0}' is public in a module assembly

data.name: MOD0001_Description
data.value: A module's types are an implementation detail: nothing outside it may reference them, and the analyzer that keeps the host free of module references depends on that. Make the type internal. Types that ASP.NET Core or EF Core must discover through reflection are exempt: controllers, page models, view components, tag helpers, and entity types configured by an IEntityTypeConfiguration in the same assembly. For anything else that genuinely has to be public, list it in modulith_allowed_public_types in .editorconfig.

data.name: MOD0002_Title
data.value: The type named by HostingStartup must be a module

data.name: MOD0002_Message
data.value: Type '{0}' is named by [assembly: HostingStartup] but does not derive from '{1}'

data.name: MOD0002_Description
data.value: ASP.NET Core will instantiate this type and cast it to IHostingStartup. Deriving from ModuleBase is what gives the module its configuration registry entry and its check that referenced modules were activated.

data.name: MOD0003_Title
data.value: The host must not use types from a module

data.name: MOD0003_Message
data.value: The host uses types from module assembly '{0}'

data.name: MOD0003_Description
data.value: The point of the model is that the host has no compile-time knowledge of any module, so that deployment topology can be chosen at startup. A project reference is fine — it only orders the build and copies the module to the output directory — but using the module's types couples the two. Move the shared type to a contracts assembly that is not itself a module.

data.name: MOD0004_Title
data.value: The host must not declare an ApplicationPart for a module

data.name: MOD0004_Message
data.value: The host declares [assembly: ApplicationPart] for module assembly '{0}'

data.name: MOD0004_Description
data.value: Application Part Discovery does not know about HostingStartup: it loads the module's controllers and pages without ever running the module's own code. Set GenerateMvcApplicationPartsAssemblyAttributes to false in the host project and let each module call AddApplicationPart for itself.

data.name: MOD0005_Title
data.value: A module must be named by an assembly-level HostingStartup attribute

data.name: MOD0005_Message
data.value: Module '{0}' is never named by an [assembly: HostingStartup] attribute and will not be loaded

data.name: MOD0005_Description
data.value: Without the attribute the module fails silently: the assembly is listed in HOSTINGSTARTUPASSEMBLIES, ASP.NET Core loads it, finds no attribute and moves on, so the module's services and endpoints simply do not exist and nothing is logged. Add [assembly: HostingStartup(typeof(YourModule))].

data.name: MOD0006_Title
data.value: A module must not replace the application pipeline

data.name: MOD0006_Message
data.value: '{0}' replaces the whole request pipeline and must not be called from a module

data.name: MOD0006_Description
data.value: IWebHostBuilder.Configure and UseStartup do not add to the pipeline, they define it — discarding whatever the host and every other module set up, including routing. A module contributes middleware by overriding ModuleBase.Configure, which runs through an IStartupFilter after the host's own pipeline is in place.

data.name: MOD0007_Title
data.value: Redundant IStartupFilter registration

data.name: MOD0007_Message
data.value: '{0}' already registers itself as an IStartupFilter

data.name: MOD0007_Description
data.value: ModuleBase registers the module as an IStartupFilter for you. Registering it again means Configure runs twice, which duplicates every piece of middleware and every endpoint the module adds — and a duplicate endpoint is an exception at startup, not a warning.

data.name: MOD0008_Title
data.value: A hosted service in a module runs in every replica that loads it

data.name: MOD0008_Message
data.value: Module '{0}' registers a hosted service, which will run once per replica of every topology that loads this module

data.name: MOD0008_Description
data.value: A worker that ran in one replica of one service now runs wherever its module is loaded, and twice if two replicas of a topology both load it. That changes behaviour silently and in production. The options are leader election, a topology that is the only one loading this module, or leaving the work outside the modular host. Suppress this once you have chosen.

data.name: MOD0020_Title
data.value: The Modulith package is not referenced

data.name: MOD0020_Message
data.value: This assembly declares a HostingStartup but does not reference '{0}', so module rules cannot be verified

data.name: MOD0020_Description
data.value: The analyzers are running without the runtime package, which means the ModuleBase type cannot be found and the rules that depend on it are silently inactive. Add a reference to the Modulith package.
